content.title: Popover: drop Copy latest segment (#793)
content.body:
Closes #793

## What

The popover loses "Copy latest segment". "Copy last dictation" and "Copy raw transcript" stay. Despite its name, the button never copied one segment: `lastFinalSegment` holds the current dictation's finished segments joined (`currentDictationEventText` as of the last final). It was therefore a less reliable copy of what "Copy last dictation" gives.

- **Paste latest segment** (`DictationSessionController.pasteLatestSegment`) had no caller: no menu item, shortcut or Settings row. It is removed with its view-model wrapper.
- **The auto-copy path stays.** In Live Auto-Paste with "Copy on stop" on, the dictation so far goes to the clipboard after each final, without touching the status line, so it holds the whole dictation at stop. It called `copyLatestSegment(updateStatus: false)`. As the only caller left, it now calls `autoCopyDictationSoFar()`, which has no status branch.
- **No settings key goes away**, so no migration is needed.
- docs/dictation.md listed an auto-copy toggle in the popover, which lives in Settings instead. It now lists the popover's copy actions.

## Proof

- `LiveAutoCopyTests` pins the kept auto-copy path: two finals write `["first part.", "first part. second part."]`, and with the setting off nothing is written. No test read the removed button or methods.
- Popover, idle state, rendered by `ViewSnapshotTests/testStatusPopoverStates` on the hosted runner: before on main ([run](https://github.com/T0mSIlver/localvoxtral/actions/runs/36271894781)), after on this branch ([run](https://github.com/T0mSIlver/localvoxtral/actions/runs/36271954625)).

  | Before | After |
  |---|---|
  | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/T0mSIlver/localvoxtral/9849504224a3815d5375274d306bf10819817441/795/popover-idle-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/T0mSIlver/localvoxtral/9849504224a3815d5375274d306bf10819817441/795/popover-idle-after.png) |

- [x] Unit suite green: hosted [`build-test`](https://github.com/T0mSIlver/localvoxtral/actions/runs/36274593200/job/108494756083) on 99f9ae1, 4582 tests. From its log:

  ```
  Test Case '-[localvoxtralTests.LiveAutoCopyTests testEachFinalCopiesTheDictationSoFar]' passed (0.008 seconds).
  Test Case '-[localvoxtralTests.LiveAutoCopyTests testWithAutoCopyOffNothingIsCopied]' passed (0.007 seconds).
  ```
- [ ] Hand check (`needs-human-review`):
  1. Install this build (`./scripts/try-pr.sh <this PR>`), open the menu bar item. Copy last dictation is followed by History (or by Copy raw transcript after a polished commit); there is no "Copy latest segment".
  2. Settings → Dictation → Output: turn on Copy on stop, pick Live Auto-Paste, dictate two sentences with a pause between them, then stop. The clipboard holds both sentences, as before this PR.

content.title: Daily minor release in place of the nightly; UI Smoke on dispatch only
content.body:
Closes #789

## Needs you

- **Which commit the gate vouches for.** The daily release ships the newest main commit on which a UI Smoke run scored the e2e dictation, normally the one you dispatch when you get home. That is main as it was at your dispatch, not main at 03:15; what merged later waits for your next dispatch. The gate itself is unchanged: a scored pass on the exact commit that gets tagged. Recommended and applied.
- **No dispatch, no release.** A day with no scored run since the last stable tag ships nothing (green, with the reason in the run summary). Recommended and applied.
- **Installer nightly channel.** `LOCALVOXTRAL_CHANNEL=nightly` now installs the newer of the newest nightly and the newest stable release. Otherwise nightly users would stay on `v0.9.1-nightly.20260926` while stable moves to 0.10.0. This reverses the old rule "never install a stable build on the nightly channel". Recommended and applied.
- **Nightly channel kept, on demand.** `release.sh nightly` still cuts an ungated prerelease of main's head, for trying a fix before the next daily. Delete it if you don't want it; I'd keep it.

## What

The 03:15 UTC cron now cuts a stable minor release (v0.9.x → v0.10.0 → v0.11.0) through the same `release.yml` pipeline and bump code as `release.sh minor`. The run happens on a new `daily` channel:

- `scripts/ci/daily-release-plan.sh` picks the commit: the newest main commit that is newer than the last stable tag and has a UI Smoke run whose `E2E dictation scored` step succeeded. The Plan step checks that commit out, so every gate builds, tags and ships it. The release is a normal stable release, so `/releases/latest` and the Homebrew cask move every day it ships.
- It skips green when main is still at the last stable tag, when no newer commit has passed the check, or when the Mac is on battery. It fails red if it cannot read the UI Smoke runs, so an unchecked commit never ships.
- `release.sh daily` does what the cron does, and `release.sh rehearse daily` rehearses it.

UI Smoke no longer has a schedule. You start it on main with the GitHub app's "Run workflow" button or `gh workflow run ui-smoke.yml`. That dispatch goes through `ui-smoke-guard.sh`, which skips green on battery or a locked screen, and a guarded run that exits 3 is also green with a warning. Branch dispatches and the label still always run and go red on exit 3. The guard dropped its "already scored in the last 20 h" rule, which only served the three-slot retry schedule.

Things that depended on the nightly channel, and what changed:
- `release.yml`: the cron now runs `daily`. The nothing-new check for scheduled nightlies is gone, because nightlies are dispatch-only and a dispatch always builds. Pruning still runs after each nightly.
- `scripts/release.sh`: new `daily` target. The client-side e2e check is skipped for it because the workflow applies the check itself.
- `scripts/install.sh`: nightly channel change, see above.
- Docs: `docs/install.md`, `docs/agent/test-tiers.md`, `.github/workflows/README.md`, and comments in `ac-power-guard.sh` and `e2e-dictation-filter.sh`.
- Unchanged: `nightly-version.sh`, `prune-nightly-releases.sh`, `resolve-release-notes.sh`, `render-cask.sh` (it already refuses nightly tags) and the nightly release body. The repo has no Sparkle or appcast feed.
- Left stale on purpose: two comments that still say "the nightly release covers main", in `ci.yml`'s `mac-lanes` job and in `mac-package-filter.sh`. Editing either file makes the lane filters run the Mac lanes for a comment.

## Proof

Linux shell suites, all green (`run-shell-suites.sh`):
```
ok      0s  scripts/ci/test-daily-release-plan.sh
ok      0s  scripts/ci/test-release-e2e-gate.sh
ok      0s  scripts/ci/test-ui-smoke-guard.sh
ok      0s  scripts/ci/test-install-resolve.sh
ok      0s  scripts/ci/test-workflow-step-names.sh
ok      0s  scripts/ci/test-ac-power-guard.sh
ok      0s  scripts/ci/test-nightly-version.sh
ok      0s  scripts/ci/test-prune-nightly-releases.sh
ok      0s  scripts/ci/test-resolve-release-notes.sh
```
`test-daily-release-plan.sh` covers these cases against a throwaway git repo and a stubbed `gh`:
```
PASS: main at the newest stable tag releases nothing and asks GitHub nothing
PASS: unscored runs are passed over; the newest scored commit ships, behind main's head
PASS: a scored run on main's head ships main's head
PASS: a scored run on an already released commit does not count
PASS: scored runs on a commit off main, unknown or malformed are ignored
PASS: a failed runs query fails closed
PASS: a failed jobs query fails closed
```
The new installer case fails on main's `install.sh` and passes with this change:
```
FAIL: nightly with a newer stable resolved 'https://github.com/T0mSIlver/localvoxtral/releases/download/v0.9.1-nightly.20260926/localvoxtral-v0.9.1-nightly.20260926.zip'
PASS: nightly moves on to a stable release newer than the last nightly
```
A read-only run of the picker against this repo today, with main at `4951dcce`:
```
base=v0.9.0
run=true
sha=26c51b809e4edcf3cd6768801047816d8396165e
reason=e2e dictation passed on 26c51b809 in UI Smoke run 36269332345; main is 2 commit(s) past it
```
If this merges today, the first daily release would be `v0.10.0` built from `26c51b80`, unless a later dispatch scores a newer commit first.

No workflow was run: this PR must not use the Mac. The full shell glob also runs on the hosted `linux` job.

Review: GLM 5.3 (cross-review, high effort) on 41dc0e97: no findings. It noted that daily releases are never pruned, and that `rehearse daily` from a branch builds the scored main commit, not the branch. Both follow from the design.

## Hand check

1. After the merge, rehearse without publishing, with the Mac free: `./scripts/release.sh rehearse daily`. The run summary should name the commit it picked and end with the `localvoxtral-release-rehearsal` artifact.
2. That evening, dispatch UI Smoke on main from the GitHub app with the Mac unlocked. Check that `E2E dictation scored` is green.
3. The next morning, check the 03:15 run: tag `v0.10.0` (or the next minor) on the commit from step 2, not a prerelease, marked latest, and the cask job green.
4. Dispatch once more with the Mac locked. The run should be green, with `E2E dictation: SKIPPED (screen is locked …)` in the summary.

content.title: Gate the control socket and WAV source on DEBUG || LOCALVOXTRAL_E2E_HARNESS (#792 step 1)
content.body:
Part of #792 (step 1 of 4). Waits for #776, which edits the control socket; this branch rebases onto it after it merges.

## What

The control socket and the WAV file that stands in for the microphone are now gated `#if DEBUG || LOCALVOXTRAL_E2E_HARNESS`, so no release build can contain them (docs/agent/invariants.md). Only the UI smoke package sets `LOCALVOXTRAL_E2E_HARNESS=1`; `LOCALVOXTRAL_DOGFOOD=1` implies it until step 3 deletes the dogfood build, because the owner's UI gate drives the dogfood app through the socket.

The capture code moves to the same condition, not just the socket: `join report` reads the capture tap, and socket replies go through the capture's redaction. Its runtime switch stays off by default, and step 2 makes it ship anyway. Debug builds therefore compile all of `Sources/localvoxtral/Dogfood`, and the ordinary unit suite now runs the dogfood suites that only the hosted `dogfood` job ran before.

`DogfoodControlBuildBoundaryTests` scanned sources for socket names outside the flag. With the socket in every debug build, that scan has nothing to check, so `package_app.sh` now searches the built binary instead (`scripts/packaging/check-harness-symbols.sh`). A release bundle fails if it holds a harness type, and a harness bundle fails if one is missing. A byte search, not `nm`, because Swift type names survive stripping in the type descriptors; the check also requires `DictationSessionController`, so a search that stopped seeing type names cannot pass.

No behavior change for release builds, the dogfood package or UI smoke.

## Proof

- [x] Unit suite green: [build-test](https://github.com/T0mSIlver/localvoxtral/actions/runs/36272044338/job/108487726085), `Executed 1495 tests, with 9 tests skipped and 0 failures`. The ordinary debug run now includes the nine suites only the `dogfood` job ran before: `DogfoodAudioFileSourceTests`, `DogfoodCaptureStoreTests`, `DogfoodCaptureRedactionTests`, `DogfoodCaptureWiringTests`, `DogfoodControlProtocolTests`, `DogfoodControlServiceTests`, `DogfoodControlSocketTests`, `DogfoodEditSignalTests`, `DogfoodBuildStatusTests` (all passed)
- [x] Symbol check on the signed release bundle ([mac-lanes packaging](https://github.com/T0mSIlver/localvoxtral/actions/runs/36276667745/job/108500686841)):
  ```
  Dogfood capture: disabled (set LOCALVOXTRAL_DOGFOOD=1 to build an instrumented artifact)
  Harness symbol check: none of 6 harness names in localvoxtral (DictationSessionController found, so the search works)
  Info.plist LVXDogfoodCapture stamp: absent
  ```
- [ ] Symbol check on the UI Smoke harness bundle, and one e2e dictation via `scripts/ui-smoke-dispatch.sh` on the final diff: waits for the owner's go (the run takes over the screen); lines go here after it
- Linux core suite (`scripts/core-tests-linux.sh`, which compiles the core's harness taps in debug): `Executed 2036 tests, with 15 tests skipped and 0 failures`
- `scripts/ci/test-harness-symbols.sh`: `harness symbol check tests: PASS`, and in build-test under the Mac's bash 3.2 (it caught `"$token×$n"`, which bash 3.2 read as one variable name; fixed by bracing) (a release binary holding any of the six names fails, a harness binary missing one fails, a file without type names fails)

Review: GLM 5.3 (opencode, high effort), 0 findings; it also ran both scripts under a real bash 3.2.

content.title: Polish with greedy decoding on the bundled helper (#563)
content.body:
**On hold.** eval-e2e scores the 4B one known-hard case lower at temperature 0 (51/159 against 52/159). The owner decides on #563 whether to merge. Details and recommendation: https://github.com/T0mSIlver/localvoxtral/issues/563#issuecomment-5830948598

## What

The bundled helper's 4B and 9B now polish with greedy decoding (temperature 0) instead of 0.3. Greedy output repeats exactly, which the evals and learning from edits (#520) need. The 0.8B keeps 0.3 because it lost a required case at 0. Mistral API, External URL and custom managed repos keep 0.3 as well: they have no catalog entry.

The temperature lives in each catalog option's `samplingDefaults`. MTP speculative decoding stays off. Production is now greedy, so the `polishd-bench` 0.3 arm sets its temperature explicitly, and the baseline arm is renamed `baseline greedy`.

Closes #563

## Proof

Main (e6d60a9f, temperature 0.3) against e4d15e87 (all three models at 0), back to back on the same Mac with the same packaged helper. The eval lane is `remote-build.sh integration-polishd [model]`; the scoreboard is `remote-build.sh eval-e2e`.

| Run | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| 4B eval-e2e | required 14/14, known-hard 52/159, errors 0 | required 14/14, known-hard 51/159, errors 0 |
| 4B eval lane (standard / agent) | required 7/7 + 1/1, known-hard 11/13 + 8/10 | identical, case for case |
| 9B eval lane (standard / agent) | required 7/7 + 1/1, known-hard 13/13 + 8/10 | required 7/7 + 1/1, known-hard 13/13 + 9/10 |
| 0.8B eval lane (standard / agent) | required 7/7 + 1/1, known-hard 8/13 + 3/10 | required 6/7 + 1/1, known-hard 6/13 + 4/10 |

- 4B eval-e2e: `b-en-semver-caret` is the only flip; greedy wrapped `^1.5` in backticks. The ASR transcripts were identical in all 159 cases.
- 0.8B: lost the required `fr-colon-missing-space`, so dfaffe3b puts it back at 0.3.
- Unit suite, `./scripts/remote-build.sh test` on e4d15e87: `4075 of 4075 tests ran in 6 shards`, 0 failures. On dfaffe3b the three suites that changed (SettingsStoreTests, PolishModelCatalogTests, PolishRequestGoldenTests) ran 121 tests, 0 failures. `SettingsStoreTests.testPolishRequestTemperature_helperGreedy_mistralAndExternalKeepDefault` asserts the request body: 0 for the 4B and 9B, 0.3 for the 0.8B, a custom managed repo, Mistral and External URL. The managed golden `16a-configuration-managed.json` now records `samplingTemperature: 0`.
- UI Smoke: not needed. `e2e-dictation-filter.sh` on this diff says `run=false`.

content.title: Overlay Buffer: polish settled pieces while the user speaks (#709)
content.body:
Closes #709

## What

In Overlay Buffer with polishing, the app now polishes the settled transcript while the user speaks, so the stop only waits for the tail. On the #709 replay (79 long dictations, GLM 5.3 on the Mistral API), the stop polish went from 1.07 s to 0.42 s median and from 4.12 s to 0.95 s at p90. Word changes stayed within the noise floor of two whole-text polishes, and none clustered at the seams. The study and the arms it rejected are in [the #709 comment](https://github.com/T0mSIlver/localvoxtral/issues/709#issuecomment-5848391453).

- `EarlyPolishPlan` (core) cuts the backend finals into pieces: whole sentences past 30 words. A period after a bare number, a single letter or inside a dotted token ends no sentence.
- `EarlyPolishRun` polishes each piece alone, one at a time, with only the templates, the reference guide and About you.
- At stop, `StopCommitCoordinator.polish` still gathers and assembles the whole-text request as before. It polishes only the tail when that request equals the bare one for the same text, the templates and endpoint match the pieces', and the prepared text starts with the pieces. Otherwise it drops the pieces and polishes the whole text. Stop-sample grounding, the dictionary, the payload macro and the spoken send cut all force the whole-text path, so learned terms, the macro and the trigger still see the whole text.
- The stop waits for the piece in flight instead of cancelling it, because polishd keeps generating a dropped request on its one slot.
- Sessions with a Mistral second pass never start early polish. Mistral's realtime stream sends no finals before the stop, and the batch text replaces the realtime text anyway.

The invariant is in `docs/agent/invariants.md`. The LLM lane filter now names the two new files.

## Proof

- Planner on Linux: `EarlyPolishPlanTests` 9/0.
- On the Mac: `DictationPipelineTests`, `EarlyPolishRunTests`, `PolishRequestGoldenTests`, `DesktopSessionPolishTests`, `DictationViewModelOverlayLifecycleTests`, `LearnedTermWiringTests`, `CopyLastDictationTests`, `DictationViewModelPolishFailureDiagnosticsTests` and `PolishTokenGuardTests`: 197 tests, 0 failures.
- `DictationPipelineTests.testOverlayBufferPolishesTheSettledPieceWhileDictatingAndOnlyTheTailAtStop` drives a real socket session. The piece is polished while dictating, and the stop sends only the tail. With `armEarlyPolish` disabled the same suite fails (`Executed 7 tests, with 6 failures`): one request for the whole text, and no piece before the stop.
- `testOverlayBufferPolishesTheWholeTextWhenTheStopGroundsItInContext`: clipboard context at stop drops the piece and polishes the whole text in one request.
- `EarlyPolishRunTests.testTheStopWaitsForThePieceInFlightAndKeepsIt`.
- Review: GLM 5.3 through Vibe (the Z.ai window was spent) passed the patch with no finding over the bar. Of its two marginal points I fixed one: `EarlyPolishPlan` sliced a string with another string's index. The other I left: the endpoint check compares URL, model and key, not sampling fields, which change only with a catalog edit in the middle of a dictation.
- Still owed: the bundled-helper replay arm (Mac slot after tonight's #568 eval), the LLM lane on this PR's CI, and one eval-e2e on the final diff.

content.title: Ship diagnostic records, on by default, under History > Storage (#792 step 2)
content.body:
Part of #792 (step 2 of 4). Stacked on #796; stays a draft until #796 is about to merge.

## What

The dogfood capture ships in every build as **diagnostic records**: one JSON file per polished Overlay Buffer dictation, on by default, with a new History > Storage row, "Keep diagnostic records on this Mac". The owner no longer needs a second, instrumented build to get them, and #518/#519 get the data from every install.

- **Keyed by History.** A record is named `dictation-<stamp>-<History id>.json` and carries that id, so it joins its entry and its audio. `saveSessionRecord` returns the id; no id (History "Don't keep", empty dictation) means no record. `DictationSessionStore` deletes records the way it deletes audio: Delete, Delete All, retention trims, and an orphan sweep at launch. The store's own limit stays 500 records and 14 days.
- **The row** sits under "Keep dictation audio on this Mac" and is built the same way: status "N records, size.", disabled under "Don't keep", and turning it off asks, then deletes the records and keeps the dictations. The group gains a Learn more link to the new docs section. No subtitle, and the popover says nothing.
- **Redaction** covers PEM private keys (also when the screen cut the block off), JWTs, `Bearer` tokens, service-prefixed keys, uppercase `…KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD…=` shell assignments and 32+ hex digits, in addition to the 43-character enrollment token. Each shape has a test, and so do the near misses it must leave alone (prose "bearer", `let apiKey = …`, short hashes).
- **The prompt sent to the agent.** The joined session's context carries `latestPriorUserPrompt` ("previous request to the agent: …") into the rendered prompts and the agent excerpt, so the old dogfood records stored it. The builder now replaces its lines in every context field before the record exists; `docs/dictation.md` promises the app never saves that prompt. Earlier prompts can still appear in screen text, which decision 1 of #792 accepted; the user docs say so.
- Unit tests get no record store (nil without runtime services), so a default-on switch cannot make the suite write into the real Application Support folder.
- The types and folder drop "dogfood" (`DiagnosticRecord*`, `EditSignalWatcher`, `Sources/localvoxtral/DiagnosticRecords`). The About > Build row, `DogfoodBuildStatus` and record flagging (no UI in any build) are gone. The control socket and WAV source keep their names and their `DEBUG || LOCALVOXTRAL_E2E_HARNESS` gate, and the socket path is unchanged.
- Docs: a "Diagnostic records" section under History in `docs/dictation.md`, a pointer in the privacy section, `docs/agent/diagnostic-records.md` for the format and rules, and `docs/dogfood-builds.md` becomes `docs/test-harness.md` (socket and WAV only).

## Proof

- [ ] Unit suite green: hosted `build-test` (link after the run). The tests that show the behavior:
  - `DiagnosticRecordWiringTests.testPolishedCommitWritesOneAttributableRecord` (switch on by default, one record)
  - `testSwitchOffWritesNothing`, `testHistoryOffWritesNothing`
  - `testRecordIDIsTheHistoryEntryID`
  - `testRecordsAreDeletedWithTheSwitchAndWithTheirDictation` (entry delete, switch off, History off)
  - `DiagnosticRecordRedactionTests`: one test per shape, plus `testWithholdsThePriorPromptFromEveryContextField`, `testWithholdsAPromptLineTheExcerptCutShort`, `testTheBuilderWithholdsThePromptItWasGiven`
- [ ] The Storage group rendered through `docs/agent/view-snapshots.md`
- [ ] `captureMilliseconds` from 20 of the owner's real dictations, median and max (needs a build on the owner's Mac)
- [ ] Hand check (owner, on the Mac):
  1. Install this PR's build with `./scripts/try-pr.sh <this PR>`.
  2. Settings > History > Storage: the third row reads "Keep diagnostic records on this Mac", switched on, with no subtitle; Learn more opens the Diagnostic records section.
  3. Dictate twice with Overlay Buffer and polishing on. The row's status shows "2 records, … KB." and `~/Library/Application Support/localvoxtral/diagnostic-records` holds two files named with History ids.
  4. Switch it off: a dialog asks "Delete 2 diagnostic records?"; confirm, and the folder is empty while History still lists both dictations.
  5. Set Keep dictations to "Don't keep": the row greys out and switched off.

Review: Codex (high effort; GLM and Vibe failed to run), 3 findings, all fixed: a prior prompt under 8 characters escaped withholding (now matched behind its label, `testWithholdsAShortPriorPromptBehindItsLabel`); a delete could land between the switch check and the write (record writes now run on the History write queue and only while the entry exists, plus a deletion epoch for delete-all: `testARecordWaitingOnADeletedDictationIsNotWritten`, `testAWriteDecidedBeforeADeleteAllIsRefused`); a crash mid-write left a temp file no sweep removed (`testRemoveStrayFilesDeletesInterruptedWritesOnly`). Follow-up review of the fixes (Vibe, GLM 5.3): no findings.
